\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പുരികം} (purikaṁ)}{പുരികം (purikaṁ)}]{\ml{പുരികം} (purikaṁ) — an eyebrow}

\label{lesson:ML-C163-purikam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for a duck, then the Malayalam for an owl.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പുരികം}}
\textbf{\ml{പുരികം}} — \emph{purikaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}an eyebrow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പുരികം}} (\emph{purikaṁ}) may come from Sanskrit \emph{bhrū}, \textquotedblleft{}eyebrow\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9688), reshaped in the mouth, but the path is not certain.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{കൈവെള്ള} (kaiveḷḷa)}{കൈവെള്ള (kaiveḷḷa)}]{\ml{കൈവെള്ള} (kaiveḷḷa) — a palm (of the hand)}

\label{lesson:ML-C163-kaivella}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for an owl, then the Malayalam for an eyebrow.

\emph{Rātri}, \textquotedblleft{}night\textquotedblright{}: which Hindi word shares its Sanskrit source? (\emph{Rāt}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{കൈവെള്ള}}
\textbf{\ml{കൈവെള്ള}} — \emph{kaiveḷḷa} — \textquotedblleft{}a palm (of the hand)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{കൈവെള്ള}} (\emph{kaiveḷḷa}) is native Dravidian, \textquotedblleft{}the white of the hand\textquotedblright{}: \emph{kai}, \textquotedblleft{}hand\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 2023), and \emph{veḷḷa}, \textquotedblleft{}white\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5496, with Tamil \emph{veḷ}). The palm is the paler side of the hand.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}
